name: IN-04
label: Safe R

model.rationale: The district's R+15 lean, Baird's incumbency, and his large fundraising advantage over a barely funded challenger all point to a comfortable Republican win, with markets agreeing at roughly 94% Republican. No polls or expert ratings exist, so uncertainty stays moderate but the outcome is not in serious doubt.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Cox or a sudden Baird scandal would be the only plausible route to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Baird, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a west-central Indiana district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. He enters the general election after easily securing renomination, with roughly $92,000 on hand and more than half a million dollars in outside support on his side of the ledger. His Democratic challenger, Drew Cox, has raised only about $20,000, leaving him with minimal resources to compete.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets put the Republican's chances at about 94%. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap — all point the same direction, making this a safe Republican seat barring an unforeseen development.
